title: Add job marks (interrupted/cancelled/cancel_pending) to job.json with read and write helpers
action: In mailbox.rs add a small `pub(crate) enum Mark { Interrupted, Cancelled, CancelPending }` with `as_str()` returning exactly `interrupted` / `cancelled` / `cancel_pending` (D8 word list, afec9446) and `parse(&str)`. Add `pub(crate) fn read_mark(bee_dir: &Path, job_id: &str) -> Option<(Mark, Option<String>)>` that reads job.json fields `mark` and `mark_reason` (None when absent or unreadable), `pub(crate) fn write_mark(bee_dir, job_id, mark: Mark, reason: &str) -> Result<(), String>` that read-modify-writes job.json setting `mark`, `mark_reason`, `mark_at` (ms epoch), and `pub(crate) fn clear_mark(bee_dir, job_id) -> Result<(), String>` that removes those three keys (used when `--continue` resumes an interrupted job, D1 c943feb9). Reuse the existing `job_path` helper (mailbox.rs:65) and the file-write style already used in this module; no new dependency. Keep every existing job.json key untouched (no-new-key law: the three keys exist only while a mark holds). Add unit tests beside the existing mailbox tests: round-trip write then read for each variant, clear removes all three keys and keeps other keys, read on a job without a mark returns None, read on a missing dir returns None.

truths: write_mark then read_mark returns the same mark and reason
clear_mark leaves job.json without mark, mark_reason, mark_at and keeps every other key
Mark::as_str yields exactly interrupted, cancelled, cancel_pending
